Some sediment accumulation noted within this area, which appears to be from runoff on the upper portion of this section (Photos 17, 18).The operator has failed to maintain the access road in accordance with 102.22(a) regulations. The violations issued on 11/30/2023 (IR 3653747) and 01/10/2024 (IR 3673501) remain outstanding.

Comments: On 07/24/2024 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a routine inspection of Southwestern's (SWN's) Vanorder-Patrick (12 Pad) Well Pad in Herrick Township, Bradford County. The weather was 70 degrees and cloudy. Rain fell on the pad within the last24 hours. I arrived at 1035 hours. The site remains stabilized with greater than 70% perennial vegetative cover. There was no accelerated erosion or sedimentation observed. There are two post-construction stormwater management structures onsite. They appear to be functioning properly. Pooled water on the pad was field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) between 192.8-262 us/cm. There was no evidence of any spills or releases. There was one produced fluid tank held within secondary containment onsite. There were nine gas processing units (GPUs) held within secondary containment onsite. There were nine wells capable of producing. There were each properly tagged with the American Petroleum Institute (API) identification numbers. There were numerous temporary storage tanks held within secondary containment onsite. Violations remain outstanding at this site from a previous release. Site remediation has been performed and a Remediation Action Completion Report has been submitted to DEPs Environmental Cleanups and Brownfields program for review. The outstanding violations will be closed once attainment with Act 2 standards has be confirmed.The DEP recommends:1. Disposing of stormwater held in the secondary containment structures as soon as possible to maintain compliance with 25 PA 78a64a(e).I departed at 1135 hours.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/12/2025
Violation Code: 91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause.
Violation ID: 8245072
Permit API: 125-29170
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Cecil Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 8/12/2025
Comments: On August 12, 2025, the Department conducted an Incident Inspection of Range Resources Conner Samuel well site, located in Cecil Township, Washington County in response to a spill that was reported to the DEP hotline on 8/11/2025 at 8:44pm by Range. Accompanying on today's inspection is Range Resources representative Kevin Rudd.According to the report and Mr. Rudd, after finishing the cement job on the 4H, a flow line became over pressurized due to a valve being left closed. This resulted in a 10 cap dislodging from the flow line and releasing approximately 21 gallons of a synthetic oil based mud (SOBM) fine mist on to the graveled well pad and approximately 42 gallons on to the secondary containment. According to Range, prior to this inspection, the fine mist release was remediated in accordance with 78a66(c)(1) and disposal documents will be provided to the Department upon its receipt.At the time of this inspection, the Act 9 Sign was observed at the access road entrance with all required information posted on it, and in the on-site mailbox was the Emergency Response Plan and Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency Plan, both of which had all required components. The access road was observed to be stabilized with gravel and the well site perimeters were observed to be exhibiting at least 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the release area to be approximately 12ft x 20ft and comprised of had freshly laid gravel. No SOBM was observed on the gravel or on the secondary containment in this area at the time of this inspection. The Department utilized a conductivity meter to screen the gravel well pad in this release area, and collected soil conductivity readings of 0.0002 mS, in three different locations as well as 0.0651 mS, and 0.0028 mS. These soil conductivity readings are comparable to the background soil conductivity reading of 0.0213 mS, which was collected upslope and adjacent to the well site in a vegetated area.At the time of this inspection, the Department requested Safety Data Sheets (SDSs) for the SOBM involved in the release as well as secondary containment inspection logs. At the time of this inspection, Mr. Rudd provided the Department with the secondary containment logs and attempted to email the Department an electronic copy of the SDSs, however, that email was not received, therefore the Department is again requesting that SDSs for the SOBM be provided to the Department within 2 business days of the receipt of this inspection report.Based on observations made at the time of this inspection, it appears that Range remediated the release in accordance with 78a66(c)(1), therefore, violations are noted and immediately corrected.Transmittal of this inspection report is delayed due to an app IT error.

Comments: This administrative inspection report is in response to the receipt of analytical results for sample number 4406-019 collected on 7/18/2024 at 11:57 AM as part of inspection report #3798130 at the Tract 726 D Pad. Elevated levels of metals and chlorides in the sample analysis indicate a release of a pollutional substance.Sample 4406-019 indicated elevated concentrations of the following parameters: Aluminum - 1.6 mg/L; Barium - 11.0 mg/L; Strontium- 1.44 mg/L; Specific Conductivity- >3,230 micro-ohms/cm; Total Chloride- 600.6 mg/L (photos 1 and 2). PGE submitted an NOV response letter to the Department on August 2, 2024 which stated the following actions were taken regarding the Department's 7/18/2024 inspection: "PGE had a vac truck take up the puddled fluid immediately. A 50 X 15 X > 3 deep area of soil was then dug up and loaded into a lined roll off for sampling and disposal. PGE asserts that it was not in violation of any state or federal regulation nor was PGE acting contrary to the permit issued under the authority of the Department. It cannot be established that the puddled fluid was caused solely by any activity conducted by PGE rather than a combination of mat washing and heavy rainfall."In follow-up inspection #3801042, the Department verified that impacted material was being scraped from the site and placed into a lined rolloff container for sampling. As the volume of pollutional material released to the pad surface has not been measured or quantified, the Department recommends PGE pursue Act 2 remediation response in accordance with 78a.66. Violations noted.

The operator at the time, SWEPI LP, has since sold the well to Pennhills Resources, who is currently operating the well. Present on site for this inspection were DEP ECB representative Barry Stanton, Pennhills Resources' Stuart and Tom Morris, and SWEPI LP's Pat Bernethy, and myself. The operator has dug up the line to determine where the leak occurred, and is collecting oil on absorbent pads. Discussion was made regarding the responsibility of each party regarding remediation and reporting. Further inspection will be done on this site as necessary.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/27/2026 to TRINITY MINERAL PARTNERS LLC in Sugar Grove Township, Warren county. 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.

Report Details

Violation Code: 78.57(a) - CONTROL, STORAGE AND DISPOSAL OF PRODUCTION FLUIDS - Operator failed to collect the brine and other fluids produced during operation, service and plugging of the well in a tank, pit or a series of pits or tanks, or other device approved by the Department or Operator discharged brine or other fluids on or into the ground or into waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8272208
Permit API: 123-47186
Unconventional: No
County: Warren
Municipality: Sugar Grove Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/27/2026
Comments: This conventional well is equipped to produce with a pump jack, a site ID sign is posted on the jack. There are no surface concerns evident on the well site at this time. 2025 APR and MIA information were submitted for this well.The tank battery for Trinity Mineral Partners' Roell lease is located approximately 500 feet to the west of this well, and is accessed off of Rounds Hill Road.This tank battery consists of two earthen containments. One containment consists of two 210 bbl stock tanks and separators, there are no surface issues evident at this containment. A second earthen containment (located southwest/downslope of the aforementioned one) holds a horizontal (approximate 250 bbl capacity) steel production water tank. There is an approximate 10' x 200' area that has been recently excavated beyond the end of the spur road that is used to access the tank battery, and continues adjacent to and downslope of, the production water tank/containment and ends at the edge of the bank that runs parallel to Rounds Hill Road. Mulch has been sparsely applied across the excavated area. Deer tracks are prevalent throughout the excavated area downslope of the production water tank/containment.Water is seeping out of the southwest corner of the production water tank containment, the specific conductance (SPC) of this water is elevated (> 1000 uS/cm). The SPC of the material at (and downslope of) the southwest corner of the production water tank containment is also elevated. Elevated SPC continues to be observed in standing water and the soil within the aforementioned excavated area downslope of the production water tank containment. Beyond the excavated area, there is an approximate 50 foot section of stressed vegetation evident on the bank of Rounds Hill Road. The SPC of the soil along this section of road bank is also elevated. The SPC of the Rounds Hill Road ditch water downslope of the aforementioned area of stressed vegetation is approximately ten times higher than the ditch water upslope of this point. The Rounds Hill Road ditch water continues to have elevated SPC for another 200 feet until the ditch enters an unnamed tributary (UNT) of Jackson Run.There was no obvious discharge from the production water tank during this inspection, the prevalence of elevated SPC and stressed vegetation in the material that comprises the containment and areas downslope of the containment is indicative of production water discharges into the containment due to poor housekeeping and/or a lack of tank integrity. The evidence obtained during this inspection also indicates that the containment surrounding the production water tank was not constructed in a manner to prevent the tank contents from reaching waters of this Commonwealth.An SAC 942 water sample was collected from standing water located in the excavated area downslope of the production water tank containment.In addition to the information requested in the attached Notice of Violation, it is requested that Trinity Mineral Partners reveal how the aforementioned excavated soil was disposed and provide any supporting documentation regarding its disposal.

Comments: On May 14, 2025, an inspection was conducted at the Fred Jones well site in Independence Township, Washington County. Notice of Termination request was approved for this site on January 5, 2017. Dylan Stanley, Expand Energy Lease Operator, was onsite during this inspection. This inspection was conducted in response to soil movement on the eastern cutslope of the well pad, which was reported to the DEP by the Expand Energy representative Jared Shockey on May 7, 2025. The DEP spoke Mr. Shockey on May 12, 2025, who stated that Expand Energy recently acquired this site and discovered the reported slough on the eastern cutslope upon assessing the site after acquisition. The slough is reportedly 1.5 feet deep and 100 feet long by 40 feet wide. The operator proposes to remove the sloughed material and add R4 riprap in its place as permanent stabilization.The following was observed:The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 1). However, it appears to be heavily deteriorated with cracks forming in its reflective layer. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP) and Preparedness Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan are onsite. However, they are severely waterlogged and could not be evaluated during this inspection (see photo 2). GPU units onsite are not equipped with secondary containment. However, the wells onsite were drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a (see photo 16). The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment do not have any observable fluid leaks (see photo 17). Some rainwater was observed in the secondary containment of the production tanks (see photo 18). Well 206H appears to be equipped for production with no evidence of fluid leaks to the ground around it observed (see photo 19). The faded well tag is completely illegible (see photo 20). Comments: This conventional well is equipped for production with a pump jack. A sign labeling the API number, well name, and operator information was posted on the well.This inspection was conducted in response to a phone call from Stuart Morris, a representative from Pennhills Resources, reporting a leak which had occurred at Well 24 (API # 053-31092). Upon arrival to the site, staff from Pennhills were actively working to remediate the issue. The well had been shut in, and a hole approximately 3 feet deep and 6 feet wide was dug near the well head to determine the source of the leak. A broken line was discovered as the source of the leak and was removed and replaced during this inspection. Crude oil was evident in the hole and could be seen within the shale (fill material) of the side walls of the hole. It appears that it's traveling through the fill that was used to build the location. Crude oil appears to have traveled through the stone/fill, and then comes out on the surface in two different areas on the southwest and northwest sides of the well site. The crude oil coming to the surface on the southwest side of the well site primarily collected in a natural depression below the well site with some migrating somewhat linearly in the southwest and west direction for approximately 25 yards. There are several small depressions on the ground surface within the linear track of the migrated crude oil which appear to hold seasonal precipitation and snowmelt. The leaked crude oil can be visually observed in these depressions. The crude oil coming to the surface on the northwest side of the well site appears to have primarily collected in a natural depression below the well site with minimal travel beyond 5 yards from the natural collection point. The amount of crude oil released as a result of this incident is undetermined due to the snow cover and lack of visual surface evidence at the site. A small tributary, denoted as Bald Hill Run (HQ-CWF), flows approximately 50 yards west of the well site. Leaked crude oil on the west side of the well site was last spotted approximately 50 feet away from Bald Hill Run. Bald Hill Run did not appear to be impacted from this incident. Also, a noted wetland is approximately 50 yards from the southwest side of the well site. The leaked crude oil on the southwest side of the well site was last observed approximately 50 feet from the wetland. The wetland did not appear to be impacted from this incident.Booms and diapers were already installed upon arrival within all the depressions where crude oil was visually observed. Booms and diapers should be regularly monitored and replaced as necessary until the site is deemed remediated. It was discussed on site to create collection points and install siphons where necessary as a remediation strategy moving forward. Also, to pump out the crude oil and fluids within the hole before burying. A follow up inspection will occur to document these efforts. Follow up inspections will routinely be conducted to monitor the remediation of the release. Confirmatory field screening and/or sampling will be conducted to verify that cleanup is deemed complete.

Violation ID: 8189739
Permit API: 129-26861
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/04/2024
Comments: On June 4th, 2024 the Department conducted an Incident Inspection of Diversified's Davenport Well located in Derry Township, Westmoreland County in response to a spill that was reported to the DEP hotline on 6/4/24 at 12:04 PM (CTS 381210). Present at today's inspection is William Warfel of Diversified Energy.At the time of this inspection, William stated that at 10:30 AM on 6/4/24 while onsite at the Davenport well, they had noticed some staining on the gravel underneath the production tank valve and a large patch of dead vegetation downslope of the well site. After using measuring devices to gauge the fluid level in the production tank, it was determined that approximately 18-20 barrels had released from the production tank. William stated that prior to the Department arriving onsite, a water truck had already come and emptied the remainder of the production tank. The production tank once empty, was then moved adjacent to where it once sat so that removal of contaminated material could begin. William showed the Department a small area on the valve pipe of the production tank where they believe the leak came from. The Department observed a dried white chalky substance on this area of the valve pipe presumed to be dried brine water. William hypothesizes that the brine water travel down the shale bank adjacent to where the production tank used to sit and pooled in the once grassy lot downslope of the well site.Upon observation of the area downslope of the production tank, the Department noticed an approximately 15ft by 8ft area of dead vegetation and mud with sheeny/iridescent puddles throughout. The Department then took a soil conductivity reading upslope of the production tank in some vegetation adjacent to the well site as a background (0.1337 mS), another in the stained gravel underneath where the production tank valve hole was (1.35 mS), and then on the shale hill leading down to the now dead vegetation adjacent to well site (1.454 mS). Then the Department began taking soil conductivity readings at the bottom of this hill to gauge how wide of an area the spill impacted. A soil conductivity reading was taken in a sheeny/iridescent puddle observed in some mud that was surrounded by dead vegetation (Over range), it was evident that all areas lacking vegetation and that were visibly wet and iridescent were impacted, so the Department went to the edge of this area to determine if any vegetated areas were impacted as well. The dead vegetation looks to be a pathway of where the release may have traveled and it leads right up to a small wooded area. Soil conductivty readings were taken at the edge of the dead vegetation where it meets the wooded area (7.63mS), another taken adjacent to the previous reading in a spot that is also where the dead vegetation meets the woods (5.51 mS), in the wooden area about 1 foot from the dead vegetation (4.90 mS) and even further in the wooded area, about 3 feet in from the dead vegetation (0.1747 mS). A reading was also taken in the grass to the left of the dead vegetation (0.280 mS) to see if that grassy area was impacted as well. These soil conductivity readings subjugate that the impacted area goes beyond where you can visibly see puddles and dead vegetation. While onsite the Department let William know that areas outside of the dead vegetation area are elevated and recommended that when removing contaminated material they give themselves a buffer area larger than 3 feet in each direction. William stated that Spartan Specialty Services would be onsite soon to place impacted soil and gravel into dumpsters and that details will be provided in the Act 2 summary report. William stated that silt fences will also be installed to ensure there are not any erosion and sedimentation issues during the removal process.Based on today's inspection, violations shall be issued for this 18-20 barrel release of brine fluid onto the gravel well site and the adjacent grass lot and wooded area.

At the time of this inspection, it does not appear that any further excavation has occurred since that date. The well has been tagged with the correct DEP permit number. The well valves were closed at the time of inspection, and the 50 bbl brine tank appears to be empty. The original violations regarding the spill at the site have been superseded by the administrative order.Since the most recent inspection of this site on 2/21/2024 (Inspection Record # 3715790) there have been no changes at the site. The outstanding violations at this site remain open and are unresolved.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 5/20/2025 to CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC in Elkland Township, Sullivan county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/20/2025
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8234378
Permit API: 113-20482
Unconventional: Yes
County: Sullivan
Municipality: Elkland Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/20/2025
Comments: Arrived onsite in response to a reported release of at least 5 gallons of produced fluid. Upon arrival I met with Creston Environmental representatives and with Mike Deming of Chesapeake (Expand).While removing secondary containment puddled fluid with elevated conductivity was discovered adjacent to the northern side of the 5HC well cellar. This location is shown on the right side of the well in Photo 1 and in Photo 3. Upon further investigation a hole was discovered in the containment in that area. After discovering the fluid a vac truck was used to remove the fluid and two sumps were started on the northern and southern sides of the wellhead. The sumps encountered additional fluid at around 2.5 feet deep. Fluid has continued to be removed from the sumps. Creston provided conductivity readings for the removed fluid. The initial puddle was 1,280 microsiemens per centimeter (uS/cm). The fluid collecting in the sumps was around 14,780 uS/cm on the northern side and 10,446 uS/cm on the southern side. Soil conductivity for the pad surface beyond the sump its self ranged between 89 and 238 uS/cm. There did not appear to be any impacts on the other exposed portions of the pad or the surrounding area. There were no seeps or standing water observed in the area around the pad including in the PCSM.The sumps will be expanded to facilitate monitoring and removal of additional fluid. There will be screening and fluid removal throughout the flowback period. After flowback equipment is removed further characterization and remediation will be completed under Act 2 per Mike Deming. DEP will conduct followup inspections over the coming days and weeks to additionally asses the stability and state of the impacted and downgrade areas.The result of this inspection is Violations Noted for CSL 402(b), SWMA 301, and 78a56(a). The violations may be closed after completion of Act 2 remediation.

Since the spill was cleaned up immediately the violations are considered corrected.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: 78a53 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL AND STORMWATER MANAGEMENT - Person proposing or conducting earth disturbance activities associated with oil and gas operations failed to comply with 25 Pa. Code § 102.
Violation ID: 8184827
Permit API: 125-28816
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Cecil Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/25/2024
Comments: On April 25, 2024 the Department conducted an inspection of the Augustine George 11039 access road located in Cecil Township, Washington County in regards to a complaint received on 04/24/24 CTS # 380091. The findings are as follows: At the time of the inspection, a truck was observed opening a valve and releasing what appeared to be freshwater onto the access road. Upon investigating this release, John Hulsey of Range Resources informed the Department that this fluid is freshwater and that the purpose of releasing said freshwater is to minimize the amount of dust caused from vehicles traveling up and down the access road. The released freshwater mixed with sediment as it flowed down the access road on to N Depaoli Road, traveled along the shoulder of N Depaoli and flowed off the shoulder into according to the site plans, an unnamed intermittent tributary to Millers Run. Conductivity readings were taken in the vegetation that is now impacted by sediment laden waters and they are as follows: 0.410 mS in the sediment laden puddle created from the flow going off the shoulder of the road, 0.464 mS in the vegetation adjacent to where the previous puddle reading was taken, 0.502 mS in some vegetation that is further in the intermittent tributary, and lastly 0.157 mS upslope of the Act 9 sign as a background reading. Though these readings subjugate that freshwater is being released, it is evident that sediment is still entering Waters of the Commonwealth. While onsite, the Department notified John Hulsey about the sediment entering the Waters of the Commonwealth and advised them to promptly cease all water release dust suppression activities on the access road.The Department recommends the Operator re-evaluate their dust suppression methods or implement measures to prevent sediment laden water from entering the intermittent unnamed tributary to Miller's Run.Based on today's inspection, violations shall be issued for the discharge of sediment into Waters of the Commonwealth.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2020-02-18 to Rockdale Marcellus Llc in Liberty Twp, Tioga county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Rockdale Marcellus Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-02-18
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 877466
Permit API: 117-21999
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Liberty Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2020-02-18
Comments: An inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator of a spill of produced water to the pad surface from a cam lock fitting between a produced water tank and a battery of frac tanks. The operator estimated the volume of the spill at 15 gallons. I met with Jen Compton of Rockdale upon arriving on location. She showed me the area where the spill occurred and impacted the pad surface. She stated that the cam lock fitting on the northern-most produced water tank was found leaking on the morning of 2/17/20. She said that the produced water flowed south toward the other produced water tank. She said that some excavation was already performed but the area in front of the south produced water tank is continuously collecting fluid with elevated electrical conductivity (EC). She said that it appeared that fluid is flowing out from underneath the south produced water tank and flowing into the area in front of the tank. A vaccuum truck was present on location during this inspection and was sucking up the fluid as it seeped into the area in front of the south tank. Ms. Compton also said that there was a truck driver on location one hour before the leak was discovered which leads them to believe that the fitting leaked for 1 hour at most. I took several EC readings in front of the south produced water tank where fluid was pooling. Every EC reading was greater than 19.99 mS/cm. No other substantial volume of water was present in the area near the produced water tanks. When I looked beneath the south tank, the gravel appeared to be saturated with fluid. It appeared that the fluid pooling in front of the tank was coming from beneath the south produced water tank. The areas Ms. Compton said had already been excavated were covered with approximately one half inch of snow. These areas appeared dry other than the snow. I took a sample, #0718-160, from the area in front of the south produced water tank which were sent to the state laboratory the same day to be analyzed for SAC 942 plus Br, Li, and Al. The Department requests a justification for the reported spill volume. The Department recommends moving the south produced water tank to assess the soil beneath it and vacuum the fluid there as needed. The Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation due to the surface area of the pad which appears to have been impacted. Violations noted.

Comments: On December 22, 2023, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted an incident inspection at the EQT ARO LLC Salt Run Hunting Club Pad A Extension. EQT reported a spill of approximately 300 gallons of glycol outside of containment and onto the well pad surface on the morning of December 22, 2023. Upon arrival, DEP spoke with EQT Rick Hall and he said that a valve fitting failed on one of the dehydration units. This caused glycol to mist onto the well pad surface. The area of impact was about 60 feet by 60 feet, in an "L" shape due to the dehydration equipment being in place. The depth of the impact to the well pad surface was unknown at the time of the inspection. Excavation of the area had not begun while DEP was onsite. EQT was waiting on equipment to be delivered to the well pad to begin the excavation around the dehydration unit and gas lines. A plan was still being developed by EQT to clean off the equipment that the glycol came in contact with. EQT plans to have Penn E and R begin the Act 2 remediation process. DEP spoke with Mr. Hall on December 26, 2023. The equipment that the glycol came in contact with was washed down. Mr. Hall said that the excavation of the impacted area was completed late on December 22, 2023. Confirmatory samples were collected and Mr. Hall provided DEP with pictures of the excavated area. The spill of glycol outside of containment onto the well pad surface is a violation of the Clean Streams Law 402(b), Solid Waste Management Act Section 301, and Chapter 78a.56(a).

Inspection Date: 6/01/2026
Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted to document observations related to the work that has been completed following the recent excavation at the secondary containment area located near the Warrant 4917 4917 156 OG Well.The excavated area downslope of the containment area where the three test holes existed previously has been roughly filled in. One of the two contaminated soil stockpiles has been moved from its previous location, but it is unclear where the contaminated soil was relocated to. The other contaminated soil stockpile remains in the containment area in its original location, and it appears to match previously observed dimensions with no noticeable sign of disturbance. Neither soil stockpile was placed on a liner or in a lined container, covered or protected in any way at any time during the cleanup effort. Soil in the area downslope of the location where the relocated stockpile once sat was found to have elevated specific conductance in excess of 1,000 micro Siemens per centimeter. Given the findings of this inspection, it does not appear that cleanup efforts are completed. In addition, the Department has not received a Final Report demonstrating attainment of a remediation standard referenced in the October 24, 2024 COA. FAE remains in violation of the October 24, 2024 COA.
